functions.funcDef: Produce and control thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).
functions.subDef: Four podded turbofans on pylons provide thrust for all phases of flight, controlled by dual-channel FADEC (SDD §5.1.1, §5.1.2).

functions.funcDef: Produce and control thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).
functions.subDef: Deploy reverse thrust on the two inboard engines for ground deceleration, inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement (SDD §5.1.2).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the flight envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Position the all-moving trimmable horizontal stabiliser and elevators for pitch control, with mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim (SDD §5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the flight envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Position two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers for roll control (SDD §5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the flight envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Position the split upper/lower rudder segments for directional control; sizing case is an outboard engine failure at V1 at maximum blade payload (SDD §5.3.2, §5.3.3).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the flight envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Drive double-slotted Fowler flaps and full-span leading-edge slats via two power drive units through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes (SDD §5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, and provide ground deceleration and directional control (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: One twin-wheel nose unit and six three-wheel main bogies support the aircraft and spread footprint pressure for semi-prepared surface flotation; retraction on HYD A with free-fall alternate (SDD §5.6.1, §5.6.2).

functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, and provide ground deceleration and directional control (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Carbon multi-disc braking, normally from HYD B, alternately HYD A, with accumulator-supported emergency braking and per-wheel-pair anti-skid; 1,800 m landing requirement is the sizing case (SDD §5.6.2, §5.6.3).

functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, and provide ground deceleration and directional control (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Hydraulic nose-wheel steering commanded from tillers and rudder pedals, with a mechanical disconnect for towing (SDD §5.6.2).

functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in access to the hold and restrain a single blade of up to 72.6 t through all flight and ground load cases (SDD §5.7.1, §5.8.1).
functions.subDef: Upward-hinging visor opens/closes hydraulically (HYD A, electric backup) with twelve latches and eight independent locking pins on a separate supply, dual dissimilar lock sensing, and a pressure interlock (SDD §5.7.1, §5.7.2).

functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in access to the hold and restrain a single blade of up to 72.6 t through all flight and ground load cases (SDD §5.7.1, §5.8.1).
functions.subDef: Nine saddles with two tension straps each restrain the blade longitudinally; lateral/vertical restraint by saddle geometry; a single instrumented tension loop monitors every strap (SDD §5.8.1, §5.8.2). Hold floor hard points are structure and excluded.

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air, control fuselage pressure differential, and supply crew breathing oxygen (SDD §5.9.1, §5.13.1).
functions.subDef: Two air-cycle packs supplied from four engines through a cross-bleed manifold condition and distribute air to the separate flight-deck and hold zones (SDD §5.9.1, §5.9.2).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air, control fuselage pressure differential, and supply crew breathing oxygen (SDD §5.9.1, §5.13.1).
functions.subDef: Two digital controllers drive two outflow valves (either sufficient) with a pneumatic backup and independent mechanical relief; hold sized to a low differential (~8,800 m equivalent, preliminary) (SDD §5.9.2).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air, control fuselage pressure differential, and supply crew breathing oxygen (SDD §5.9.1, §5.13.1).
functions.subDef: Two high-pressure cylinders on a common manifold with crossover feed four quick-donning masks for depressurisation, smoke and fume events and the subsequent diversion (SDD §5.13.1, §5.13.2).

functions.funcName: Protect the aircraft from fire and ice
functions.funcDef: Detect and extinguish fire/overheat where required, and prevent or remove ice accretion within the icing envelope (SDD §5.12.1, §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Detect and extinguish fire and overheat
functions.subDef: Dual-loop continuous detection in each engine nacelle and APU with degraded single-loop logic; two cross-plumbed bottles per engine pair; overheat detection on bleed ducts and gear bays; hold smoke detection with no suppression (SDD §5.12.1, §5.12.2).

functions.funcName: Protect the aircraft from fire and ice
functions.funcDef: Detect and extinguish fire/overheat where required, and prevent or remove ice accretion within the icing envelope (SDD §5.10.1, §5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Bleed-air anti-ice to wing leading edges and engine cowls, electrically heated stabiliser zones and probes/windshields, with two ice detectors advisory and manual/automatic activation (SDD §5.10.1, §5.10.2).

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the failure alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subName: Acquire, process and present flight data
functions.subDef: Four display units and two head-up displays on three display processing units over dual deterministic networks, three air-data inertial reference units, dual FMS/nav, and an independent standby instrument on the DC essential bus (SDD §5.11.1, §5.11.2).

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the failure alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures, driven by two independent processing channels (SDD §5.11.2).

Hull loss is credited as not recoverable by crew action.
fha.effCrew: Multiple fatalities / crew incapacitation — the crew are aboard and the loss is not recoverable (joint top-step effect).
fha.effPax: Multiple fatalities — flight crew aboard; the top step is joint with the aircraft loss.
fha.judgementNote: Crew workload level for the in-flight unlock is on the joint top step, so no HF timing is needed for the class; flagged because the malfunction's manifestation (an unlock command running in flight versus a lock failing to hold under load) is assumed to defeat the interlock/lock chain — if the lock pins and pressure interlock reliably prevent any in-flight visor release, exposure and detectability move but the end-state class stands.

fha.effCrew: Ground crew must recognise and re-secure; potential ground injury hazard from an unexpectedly moving visor, but flight crew workload unaffected and dispatch is inhibited by the lock-status/take-off configuration check.
fha.effPax: No occupants aboard for a ground unlock; hold unoccupied.
fha.judgementNote: Crew level assumed pending the HF workload; assumed the flight-deck lock-status indication and take-off configuration check reliably prevent dispatch with the visor unsecured — if that detection is not credited, a ground unlock could persist into taxi/take-off and inherit the in-flight Catastrophic class.

fha.effAc: No degradation of the airframe itself, but with all crew oxygen lost the aircraft has no protection for its two-crew complement against a depressurisation, smoke or fume event; a subsequent pressurisation loss or smoke event at FL260 would leave the flight crew without breathing protection during the emergency descent and diversion — a large reduction in functional capabilities to cope with that adverse condition.
fha.effCrew: With no supplemental oxygen the flight crew cannot be relied upon to perform an emergency descent and diversion accurately in a hypoxic or smoke environment — physical distress or excessive workload such that the flightcrew cannot be relied upon to perform their tasks. fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no passenger oxygen fitted, so no direct occupant effect.

fha.fcDesc: Total loss of fire and overheat detection
fha.phases: Standing, Taxi, Takeoff, Initial Climb, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing, Rejected Takeoff, Go-around
fha.effAc: No detection of fire or overheat in the engine nacelles, APU compartment, bleed-duct runs, main gear bays or hold; a fire could develop and propagate undetected in a fire zone containing engine, fuel and high-energy sources, defeating the crew's ability to respond and extinguish in time — a large reduction in safety margins, with an undetected nacelle or hold fire able to progress to loss of the airplane.
fha.effCrew: With no detection the crew receive no warning of a developing fire and cannot initiate the fire drill; workload becomes excessive once secondary symptoms appear, by which time margins are severely eroded — physical distress or excessive workload such that the crew cannot be relied upon to respond in time.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no direct occupant effect, though an undetected hold or nacelle fire threatens the whole airframe.

Committed to flight, the aircraft must divert and descend out of icing; where icing cannot be avoided this progresses toward a large reduction in safety margins.

Crew level assumed pending HF workload. Confirm with the icing operational envelope and IPS MAC.

fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant effect.

fha.effAc: Undetected loss of payload restraint with the aircraft standing produces no load excursion; restraint tensioning and checks are a ground procedure completed before departure, so any loss is caught during loading rather than propagating.
fha.effCrew: Restraint status is available on the flight deck and part of the pre-flight/take-off configuration check; crew catch the condition on the ground.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant effect while standing.

assumptions.text: The aircraft-level function list and its top-function groupings are a derived reading of the SDD, not stated by the document.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly states it does not enumerate aircraft-level functions; grouping fourteen systems into seven functions was forced by the absence of a stated function list.
assumptions.ifWrong: The top-function boundaries and one-level split change; sub-functions may re-parent, merge or split, altering downstream AFHA function/FC allocation.
assumptions.usedFor: All seven top functions and their nineteen sub-functions.

citations.quote: It does not tell you what the aircraft-level functions are.

assumptions.text: FUE, HYD, EPS and EWS are resources consumed by functions and are deliberately NOT authored as aircraft functions.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD classifies these four systems as resources that supply other systems rather than act on the aircraft; the modeling rule excludes resources as functions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any resource must be modeled as a function, an additional top-level function and its decomposition would be added.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS from the function set.

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft

assumptions.text: The nose-door load path and hold-floor hard points are structure and are excluded from the functional decomposition.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the door is a single load path treated as structure and there is no redundancy in the hold hard points; structure is substantiated by structural/particular-risk analysis, not functional FHA.
assumptions.ifWrong: If structural integrity were to be captured functionally, additional items would appear under Load and secure payload; this would be non-conforming to the modeling rule.

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure

assumptions.text: The Aware/Unaware split for the control axes assumes some erroneous or uncommanded surface behaviour can develop below crew detection thresholds before annunciation.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists FCS status/discretes as outputs but gives no detection thresholds or annunciation timing, so the undetectable subset cannot be bounded from the provided inputs.
assumptions.ifWrong: If all erroneous/uncommanded axis behaviour is intrinsically evident, the SF-003/004/005 Unaware rows collapse and only Aware rows remain.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003 Unaware, SF-004 Unaware, SF-005 Unaware

citations.quote: Surface position and system status to the avionics displays; flight envelope protection status; asymmetry and jam discretes

assumptions.text: Reverse thrust is treated as an aircraft-level deceleration capability whose inadvertent in-flight case is a distinct malfunction condition despite the WoW/radalt inhibit.
assumptions.rationale: The function list names 'Provide reverse thrust' as its own sub-function; the inhibit is a mitigation, not proof the inadvertent condition cannot occur, so it stays a candidate condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the inhibit is shown fully defeating in-flight deployment, the SF-002 inadvertent-reverse conditions move entirely to the ground phase in the FHA.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002 Aware inadvertent reverse thrust, SF-002 Unaware

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock

assumptions.text: Partial loss of propulsive thrust includes an asymmetric variant distinct from a symmetric power reduction.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD makes asymmetric outboard thrust the directional-control sizing case, so an asymmetric partial loss is functionally distinct and must be its own condition — but stays implementation-agnostic at aircraft level.
assumptions.ifWrong: If asymmetry is not a distinguishable aircraft-level capability loss, the SF-001 asymmetric partial merges into the single partial-loss condition.

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: The MAC dividing Total from Partial loss for SF-006/007/008/009 is not yet frozen, so within-MAC vs outside-MAC splits are read conservatively at aircraft level.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the gear-leg/bogie count and hold differential are preliminary and not frozen, so no MAC is settled for these ground and high-lift functions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a MAC is later defined, some Partial-loss conditions may reclassify as Total loss (outside MAC) or vice versa, changing the FCIM cell content.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006, SF-007, SF-008, SF-009 Total/Partial-loss rows

citations.quote: The number of gear legs and bogies is preliminary design data and is not frozen.

assumptions.text: Erroneous high-lift position and asymmetric high-lift can develop below crew detection thresholds and therefore warrant a crew-unaware consideration, though asymmetry braking is fitted.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names asymmetry brakes but gives no aircraft-level annunciation detail, so the undetected-development case cannot be dismissed for the whole function.
assumptions.ifWrong: If asymmetry is always annunciated, the crew-unaware variant collapses and the malfunction set stays Aware-only.

citations.quote: asymmetry brakes at each section

assumptions.text: A ground-deceleration or ground-directional malfunction can develop undetected below crew thresholds during the ground roll, warranting a crew-unaware row.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes continuous brake-temperature monitoring but does not establish that a slow-onset deceleration or steering deviation is annunciated at aircraft level.
assumptions.ifWrong: If all such deviations are annunciated, the unaware rows for SF-008 and SF-009 are inapplicable and should be removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-008 unaware row, SF-009 unaware row

citations.quote: Brake temperature is monitored continuously and a turnaround limit is displayed.

assumptions.text: The Minimum Acceptable Configuration for these five functions is not yet defined, so Total vs Partial loss is read conservatively.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes redundancy but does not state the minimum configuration required for continued safe flight and landing for these functions.
assumptions.ifWrong: The Total/Partial boundary shifts and conditions may migrate between the Total loss and Partial loss cells.
assumptions.usedFor: All Total loss and Partial loss cells for SF-011, SF-012, SF-013, SF-014, SF-015

citations.quote: The hold differential and the gear leg and bogie count in particular are not frozen

assumptions.text: The crew-unaware variant of SF-014 is inapplicable because cylinder pressure is displayed continuously and low-pressure alerting is provided.
assumptions.rationale: SDD grounds continuous indication and alerting; no undetectable-below-threshold mode was identified for crew oxygen.
assumptions.ifWrong: A crew-Unaware row for SF-014 must be added carrying any undetectable supply-degradation condition.

citations.quote: cylinder pressure and system status to the flight deck; low pressure alerting

assumptions.text: The single instrumented tension monitoring loop can fail such that restraint loss develops without annunciation.
assumptions.rationale: SDD records the monitoring loop as a single loop whose coverage is a recorded item, supporting an undetected condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-011 Unaware row (Undetected loss of payload restraint) would be removed.

citations.quote: The restraint tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented loop and its coverage is a recorded item

assumptions.text: Contamination of conditioned air is a distinct undetected malfunction of SF-012 not covered by the provided monitoring.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD does not describe air-quality or contamination detection for the conditioning system, so detection cannot be grounded.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-012 Unaware malfunction may be detectable and would move to the Aware row, or be deleted if not a credible condition.

assumptions.text: Loss or partial loss of ice protection can develop without a corresponding annunciation because the two ice detectors are a single common type.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD annunciates lost electrical zones but detection relies on two identical detectors whose commonality is flagged, so a detector-common-mode failure could leave a real loss undetected.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-016 Unaware row would collapse into the Aware row and the undetected conditions would drop out.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-016 Unaware row (Undetected loss / Undetected partial loss of ice protection)

citations.quote: The two ice detectors are identical in type and their commonality is recorded as an item for examination.

assumptions.text: Erroneous or misleading flight data can be presented below crew detection thresholds despite three reference units, warranting a distinct crew-Unaware row.
assumptions.rationale: The provided material describes triple reference units and a standby instrument but gives no detection-coverage or monitoring threshold data, so undetected erroneous output cannot be dismissed.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-017 Unaware malfunction row would be removed and only the Aware erroneous/misleading conditions would remain.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-017 Unaware row (Undetected erroneous / Undetected misleading flight data)

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data.

assumptions.text: A loss of the crew alerting function may itself be unannunciated, so SF-018 carries a crew-Unaware row for the undetected loss cases.
assumptions.rationale: The alerting function is the aircraft's own detection means; the provided material does not state a monitor that annunciates loss of alerting, so the un-annunciated case must be retained.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-018 Unaware row would be removed if a substantiated self-monitor annunciates loss of the alerting function.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018 Unaware row (Undetected loss / Undetected partial loss of crew alerting)

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.text: Total loss of propulsive thrust in flight is not recoverable and results in hull loss.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states propulsion provides thrust for all phases of flight but does not describe any means of sustaining flight with all four engines lost.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any credited means sustains flight with all engines out, the in-flight SF-001-TL row drops from Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: Total loss of propulsive thrust (in-flight row)

citations.quote: Four podded turbofans on pylons beneath the high wing provide thrust for all phases of flight

assumptions.text: Partial loss of propulsive thrust is bounded by the single-engine-out design dispatch case, allowing continuation to a suitable aerodrome.
assumptions.rationale: No MAC rule yet defines how many engines must remain; the SDD gives the one-engine-out continue case but states a second same-side loss is outside the design dispatch case.
assumptions.ifWrong: If 'partial loss' encompasses a second same-side engine loss, the SF-001-PL air row escalates above Major toward Hazardous/Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: Partial loss of propulsive thrust (air row)

citations.quote: designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following the loss of any one engine at or after V1

assumptions.text: Erroneous and uncommanded thrust are bounded to a single engine and remain within the rudder authority sized for the outboard-engine asymmetry, and the crew detect and arrest the excursion.
assumptions.rationale: No timed crew task or MAC rule exists yet to establish detectability and controllability of the asymmetry; the directional-control sizing case is stated but the recovery credit is not yet substantiated.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the erroneous/uncommanded thrust exceeds controllable authority or is not arrested in time, the air rows of SF-001-M and SF-001-M2 escalate to Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: Erroneous thrust response to command (air row); Uncommanded thrust change (air row)

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: An undetected erroneous thrust response in flight can diverge beyond controllable authority before crew cues permit recovery, per the loss-of-annunciation rule.
assumptions.rationale: §5.4.2 requires the combination of a failure with loss of its annunciation to meet the objective of the un-annunciated effect, but no annunciation-coverage or HF timing analysis yet exists for this state.
assumptions.ifWrong: If flight-deck physical cues reliably substitute for the lost annunciation, the in-flight SF-001-M3 row drops from Catastrophic to Hazardous.

citations.quote: Each engine carries a full-authority digital engine control with dual redundant channels

assumptions.text: A total thrust loss on take-off is assumed to occur at or before V1 so the take-off is rejectable.
assumptions.rationale: The reject decision point (V1) and a timed reject task are not yet established; the go/stop boundary determines whether the take-off phase is escapable.
assumptions.ifWrong: If total thrust is lost after V1, the take-off phase of SF-001-TL is not escapable and carries the hull-loss end effect (Catastrophic) rather than Major.
assumptions.usedFor: Total loss of propulsive thrust (Takeoff/Rejected Takeoff row)

citations.quote: continue to a suitable aerodrome following the loss of any one engine at or after V1

assumptions.text: An undetected uncommanded thrust change at the outboard 28 m moment arm produces an asymmetric upset that the crew, being unaware, do not counter promptly.
assumptions.rationale: The FCIM condition is 'undetected', so no crew recognition/response can be credited, and no HF task timing is provided.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detection coverage or directional authority makes the asymmetry benign or promptly counterable, SF-001-M4 airborne/take-off rows drop from Hazardous toward Major.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001-M4 Takeoff/Rejected Takeoff row; SF-001-M4 in-flight row

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: Wheel braking alone achieves the required landing distance on the semi-prepared strip, so total loss of reverse thrust erodes but does not defeat the rollout margin.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives a 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout but no braking-only landing distance on the unpaved surface.
assumptions.ifWrong: If braking-only distance exceeds the 1,800 m requirement on the semi-prepared surface, SF-002-TL Landing rises from Major to Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002-TL Landing row; SF-002-PL Landing row

citations.quote: landing distance requirement is 1,800 m (6,000 ft) on such a surface. Predicted landing rollout... approximately 1,080 m

assumptions.text: The in-flight reverser inhibit (weight-on-wheels + radio-altimeter agreement + mechanical sleeve lock) precludes uncommanded in-flight deployment, so inadvertent reverse thrust is limited to a significant, not catastrophic, upset.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the inhibit exists but the independence/coverage of the interlock is not analysed here; this belongs to the PSSA.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the interlock does not preclude in-flight deployment, SF-002-M in-flight rises from Major toward Hazardous or Catastrophic.

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock

assumptions.text: Reverse thrust is used only on landing rollout, so all SF-002 conditions have no effect on the aircraft in every phase before landing rollout.
assumptions.rationale: Standard reverser operating concept; the SDD confirms reversers are inhibited in flight but does not restate the ground-only usage explicitly.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any reverse-thrust demand exists before landing rollout, the No Safety Effect pre-landing rows for SF-002-TL/PL/M2 would need reclassification.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002-TL pre-landing NSE row; SF-002-PL pre-landing NSE row; SF-002-M2 pre-landing NSE row

assumptions.text: The in-flight thrust-reverser inhibit (weight-on-wheels + radio-altimeter agreement + mechanical sleeve lock) reliably prevents inadvertent reverser deployment in flight.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the inhibit exists but provides no integrity or failure data; the in-flight severity of SF-002-M3 turns entirely on whether the inhibit can be defeated.
assumptions.ifWrong: The 'Undetected inadvertent reverse thrust — in-flight' row rises from No Safety Effect to a thrust-asymmetry case, potentially Hazardous or Catastrophic in the low-speed phases.

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve.

assumptions.text: An undetected inadvertent reverse-thrust excursion on the ground is arrestable by the crew within the available runway margin (predicted 1,080 m rollout against the 1,800 m requirement) on a semi-prepared strip.
assumptions.rationale: No HF task analysis or ground-directional-control study is provided; the Major class depends on the excursion being recoverable.
assumptions.ifWrong: The on-ground SF-002-M3 row rises from Major toward Hazardous if the asymmetric excursion cannot be arrested within the strip margin.

citations.quote: predicted landing rollout is approximately 1,080 m, and the margin between the two is the basis

assumptions.text: 'Total loss of pitch control' means loss of all pitch-command paths including the mechanical stabiliser-trim reversion, i.e. no surviving means of pitch control.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes a mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim; the total-loss classification requires clarifying that reversion is exhausted, and no MAC rule for pitch exists yet.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a surviving reversion path is credited with sufficient pitch authority, the true 'total loss' state is deeper in the tree but remains Catastrophic; the row would instead read as partial loss of that reversion.

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.text: A full-authority erroneous or uncommanded pitch excursion in a critical (low-altitude/high-speed) phase is not arrested before departure from the flight envelope.
assumptions.rationale: The fly-by-wire monitor coverage and response time and the mechanical reversion effectiveness against a hardover are not quantified in the SDD; the Catastrophic worst-phase class depends on the excursion being unbounded.
assumptions.ifWrong: If dissimilar-computer voting and a fast monitor bound the excursion below envelope departure, the worst-phase class for SF-003-M and SF-003-M2 reduces toward Hazardous.

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.text: Partial loss of pitch authority leaves pitch controllable and requires at least one further independent failure to reach total loss (dual actuation per surface on different hydraulics).
assumptions.rationale: No MAC rule for pitch and no HF workload data exist yet; the Hazardous/Major grading of the partial-loss rows depends on residual authority and remaining margin to catastrophe.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single partial-loss condition materially compromises pitch controllability, the partial-loss rows rise toward Catastrophic; if the degradation is trivial and dispatch-recoverable they fall to Minor.

citations.quote: Every primary surface is driven by at least two actuators supplied from different hydraulic systems.

assumptions.text: An undetected erroneous or uncommanded pitch response cannot be detected and arrested by the crew from raw flight-path cues before loss of control.
assumptions.rationale: No timed crew task / HF workload analysis exists yet for detecting an unannunciated pitch error.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-003-M3 and SF-003-M4 airborne rows would drop below Catastrophic (toward Hazardous) if timely detection and recovery are credited.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-M3 and SF-003-M4 airborne Catastrophic rows

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.text: No MAC rule yet defines a survivable minimum roll configuration, and total loss of both aileron hydraulic supplies plus spoilers leaves no usable lateral control (no roll mechanical reversion).
assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists a mechanical reversion path for stabiliser trim and lower rudder only, not for roll, and no MAC rule is provided.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-004-TL would fall below Catastrophic if a MAC or reversion path leaves usable lateral control.

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.text: After a partial loss of roll authority the dual-actuation architecture leaves roll authority sufficient to manage the flight and continue to a landing with increased crew effort.
assumptions.rationale: No MAC rule quantifies remaining roll authority after a partial loss; the SDD only states dual actuation from different hydraulics.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-004-PL would rise to Hazardous if the credited partial state leaves authority below the sizing gust/crosswind requirement.

citations.quote: Every primary surface is driven by at least two actuators supplied from different hydraulic systems

assumptions.text: The worst credited erroneous roll response is full-authority / wrong-sense and, at a critical low-altitude phase, is not recoverable within the time available.
assumptions.rationale: No magnitude/rate limit on the erroneous command and no timed crew reaction task are provided.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-004-M airborne row would fall to Hazardous if the erroneous command is bounded/rate-limited and crew recovery is credited.

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.text: An aware uncommanded or erroneous roll (SF-004-M2/M3/M4) can be arrested by the crew outside the low-altitude corner but is not guaranteed recoverable at low altitude/near surface, keeping the class at Hazardous rather than Catastrophic.
assumptions.rationale: No HF workload analysis or timed crew recovery task exists yet, and no MAC defines residual roll authority after these conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If low-altitude recovery cannot be shown, SF-004-M2/M3/M4 escalate toward Catastrophic in the takeoff/approach/landing/go-around phases, splitting each into a low-altitude Catastrophic row.

citations.quote: Roll is by two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers

assumptions.text: The undetected roll conditions (SF-004-M3/M4) are detectable by attitude cues but late, with no automatic alerting credited, so the un-annunciated effect governs and holds them at Hazardous.
assumptions.rationale: No alerting coverage or detection-time data is provided for these conditions and AC 25.1309-1B §5.4.2 requires the un-annunciated effect to govern.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an undetected roll can develop to departure before any perception, SF-004-M3/M4 become Catastrophic; if FCS monitoring makes undetected roll implausible they trend Major.

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.text: 'Total loss of yaw control' means all rudder authority including the mechanical reversion path to the lower rudder segment is lost, so no survivable degraded directional means remains.
assumptions.rationale: No MAC rule exists yet defining what constitutes total loss of yaw for this split-rudder-with-reversion architecture.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the mechanical reversion to the lower rudder segment always survives, SF-005-TL is not truly total and the class drops from Catastrophic to Hazardous.

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.text: Total loss of directional control is not survivable against the directional-control sizing case (outboard engine out at V1 with max blade payload at a 28 m moment arm), making SF-005-TL Catastrophic in the airborne phases.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names the outboard-engine-out case as the directional-control sizing case but no fault tree or MAC quantifies survivability with zero rudder authority.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a survivable means of directional control exists without rudder authority, SF-005-TL is Hazardous rather than Catastrophic.

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: After a partial loss of yaw authority sufficient directional control remains for the non-critical case but the engine-out sizing case is degraded, keeping SF-005-PL at Hazardous rather than Major or Catastrophic.
assumptions.rationale: No MAC defines residual rudder authority after a single-supply loss for the split-segment arrangement.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the engine-out directional case is still fully met after partial loss, SF-005-PL is Major; if a partial loss coincident with engine-out is uncontrollable it is Catastrophic.

citations.quote: a single rudder supply loss must still leave sufficient authority

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only, so all occupant-axis effects reduce to the flight crew aboard.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the hold is not occupied in flight; occupant axes must be set relative to crew only.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried, occupant-axis levels on every row would need independent assessment and could raise some classes.

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: With crew detection removed, an erroneous or uncommanded yaw is not bounded by design authority limits and progresses to loss of control in directional-critical phases.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the split-rudder architecture and asymmetry/jam discretes but does not state the maximum authority of an erroneous rudder command or whether it is self-limiting.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-005-M3 and SF-005-M4 flight-phase rows fall from Catastrophic to Hazardous.

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes

assumptions.text: A flightcrew can detect and arrest a single detected erroneous/uncommanded yaw within available time in all flight phases, keeping the outcome below loss of control.
assumptions.rationale: No HF timed-task analysis exists yet; the crew workload level is recorded as assumed pending it.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-005-M and SF-005-M2 flight-phase rows could rise from Major to Hazardous on the crew axis.

citations.quote: yaw by a split rudder in upper and lower segments, each with its own actuation

assumptions.text: A longer diversion runway is reachable such that a total flapless landing is survivable rather than an unavoidable overrun of the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m normal rollout but no flapless landing distance and no MAC rule for high-lift.

assumptions.text: Undetected partial loss of crew alerting leaves primary flight-path and immediate-hazard alerting intact and degrades a non-critical subset of the alert list.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA is pre-design and no MAC rule or crew-alerting FMEA yet defines which alerts are lost in the partial case; the class turns on whether the lost subset includes a Hazardous/Catastrophic precursor.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the lost subset includes an alert whose combined un-annunciated objective is Hazardous or Catastrophic, §5.4.2 drives the class up from Major and the row must be re-graded and split.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-PL2 row — Undetected partial loss of crew alerting

citations.quote: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only, so there is no passenger/occupant exposure axis.
assumptions.rationale: The occupant axis must be set for every row; the SDD states the hold is not occupied and the complement is crew-only.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried the pax axis would need re-evaluation, though for a latent alerting loss it would remain the non-driving axis.

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: Aircraft and crew effect levels (significant / significant) are provisional pending the MAC coverage rule and the HF workload task analysis.
assumptions.rationale: The task states no MAC rule and no timed crew task exist yet for SF-018-PL2, so both driving levels are recorded as assumed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the MAC requires higher residual coverage, or the HF analysis shows the degraded monitoring burden is only slight, the class could move to Hazardous or Minor respectively.
